title: Correct frictional force magnitude (1)
description: Essential: The student must state that the frictional force in part (1) is 6 N.

title: Correct frictional force direction (1)
description: Essential: The student must correctly identify the direction of the friction in part (1) (e.g., to the right).

title: Correct frictional force magnitude (2)
description: Essential: The student must state that the frictional force in part (2) is 6 N.

title: Correct frictional force direction (2)
description: Essential: The student must correctly identify the direction of the friction in part (2) (e.g., to the left).

title: Correct frictional force magnitude (3)
description: Essential: The student must state that the frictional force in part (3) is 8 N.

title: Correct frictional force direction (3)
description: Essential: The student must correctly identify the direction of the friction in part (3) (e.g., to the right).

title: Net force equilibrium reasoning
description: Important: The student's solution must apply Newton's first law (net force = 0) for the static equilibrium in parts (1) and (2).

title: Maximum static friction calculation
description: Important: The student must correctly calculate the maximum static friction (8 N) and compare it to applied forces.

title: Kinetic friction application
description: Important: For part (3), the student must recognize that motion occurs and correctly apply the kinetic friction formula.

title: Sign/direction confusion
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student confuses the direction of the frictional force (e.g., assigns left when it should be right).

title: Incorrect friction type
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student incorrectly uses kinetic friction for a static situation (parts 1 & 2) or static friction for a kinetic situation (part 3).
